original_question: For integers q >= p >= 3, what is the maximum spectral radius among graphs in G(m, theta_{1,p,q})? Equivalently, characterize the extremal graphs with m edges that avoid the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two endpoints.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 8, with its complete resolution supplied nearby by Theorem 3.27 and Theorem 3.36.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the forbidden graph family as theta graphs of the form θ_{1,p,q}, uses the paper’s class notation 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}), asks for the extremal adjacency spectral radius at fixed edge size m, and asks for the extremal graphs attaining that maximum. Those are exactly the core ingredients of Problem 8 in the survey’s theta-graph discussion.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient graph class is finite, simple, undirected graphs; this is set globally in Section 1.
The notation 𝒢(m,F) is not just 'graphs with m edges avoiding F': it means F-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices.
The spectral radius is the adjacency spectral radius λ(G), i.e. the largest eigenvalue of the real symmetric adjacency matrix A(G).

In the survey, the broad question is posed as Problem 8, but the actual complete answer is split into two cases: the special case (p,q)=(3,3) and the remaining cases handled by parameterizing p+q as 2k+1 or 2k+2.
The special case θ_{1,3,3} is treated separately in Theorem 3.27, with the explicit condition m ≥ 43.
The general case is not stated for arbitrary small m: Theorem 3.36 requires an integer k ≥ 3 and the explicit lower bound m ≥ (9/4)k^6 + 6k^5 + 46k^4 + 56k^3 + 196k^2.

The general case also requires the hidden quantifier that either p+q = 2k+1 or r+s = 2k+2; equivalently, the theorem groups θ_{1,p,q}-free and θ_{1,r,s}-free graphs by the sum of the two longer path lengths.
The extremal graph form is implicit in your draft but not stated: in the general case it is K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k-1)/2)K_1, and in the special case (p,q)=(3,3) it is K_2 ∨ ((m-1)/2)K_1.
Your draft does not reflect that the survey presents the result as a complete solution to Problem 8 only after combining Theorem 3.27 with Theorem 3.36.

The phrase 'equivalently' is a little too strong as written: the paper’s edge-spectral-Turán problem asks both for the maximum value and for the extremal graphs; characterizing extremal graphs is the companion task rather than a separately stated proved equivalence.
refined_question: Let θ_{1,p,q} denote the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q joining the same two endpoints, and let 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}) be the family of simple θ_{1,p,q}-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices. For integers q ≥ p ≥ 3, determine the maximum adjacency spectral radius λ(G) over all G ∈ 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}) and characterize the extremal graphs attaining it; in the paper’s actual resolution, this must be stated with the paper’s two-case split, namely the special case (p,q)=(3,3) with m ≥ 43, and the general case in which k ≥ 3, p+q ∈ {2k+1, 2k+2}, and m ≥ (9/4)k^6 + 6k^5 + 46k^4 + 56k^3 + 196k^2.
justification: The draft is closest to Problem 8, which asks exactly for the maximum spectral radius in 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}) for q ≥ p ≥ 3. To make that question stand alone and faithful to the survey, one must import the global definition of 𝒢(m,F) from Section 1 and the meaning of λ(G) as adjacency spectral radius. The nearby context also shows that the paper does not treat all (p,q) uniformly in one theorem: Theorem 3.27 handles θ_{1,3,3}, while Theorem 3.36 handles the remaining cases by grouping them according to p+q = 2k+1 or 2k+2 with an explicit lower bound on m. Since the survey itself says that Theorem 3.36 together with Theorem 3.27 solves Problem 8 completely, a paper-faithful stand-alone version of your draft should include that split and those thresholds rather than leave the scope implicit.
